description: ASU AstroFusion Team: students from the Applied Science University Bahrain
summary: Trade Space is a browser-based mission design game where players design, launch and evaluate a NASA-style space mission. Players choose a science goal, then balance competing constraints such as budget, mass, power and risk, just as real mission engineers make trade-offs. After launch, each mission is scored on science return, cost and reliability, so players see how every decision shaped the outcome. The game has five stages of increasing difficulty, and players must complete each stage to unlock the next. A leaderboard ranks players and teams. Four game modes are available. Offline: Solo, and Team Hot-Seat, where a full team plays together on one device. Online: Co-op, where players join friends to design a mission together, and Team vs. Team, where two teams challenge each other. Trade Space makes systems engineering accessible, social and competitive for students and the public, with no installation needed.
details:
Trade Space puts the player in the role of a mission designer. Players design a NASA-style mission, launch it, and evaluate the outcome. Because every design decision affects the result, players discover that a good mission is a balance, not a maximum. They can redesign and try again, learning from each outcome.

HOW IT WORKS

  1. Design: the player makes mission and spacecraft design choices.
  2. Launch: the mission is run and the outcome is shown.
  3. Evaluate: the player reviews how the design performed and which trade-offs shaped the result.

FIVE STAGES OF INCREASING DIFFICULTY
The game has five stages, each harder than the last. Players must complete a stage to unlock the next, so they build up their understanding of trade-offs step by step, from simpler missions to tighter constraints and higher stakes. A leaderboard ranks players and teams, encouraging them to replay stages and improve their results.

FOUR GAME MODES
Offline (no connection needed once loaded):

  • Solo: one player designs and flies missions alone.
  • Team on one device: a full team plays together on the same device, discussing and deciding every trade-off as a group, which makes it well suited to a classroom.

Online:

  • Play with friends: players join friends and design missions together.
  • Team vs. team: two teams challenge each other on the same mission, and the better balanced design wins.

WHY IT MATTERS
Trade-space analysis is how space agencies compare mission options before building anything, but it is usually hidden behind spreadsheets and specialist tools. Trade Space makes this way of thinking visible, interactive, and fun, helping students, teachers, and the public understand why space missions look the way they do.

INTENDED IMPACT
Introduce systems-engineering thinking to students and non-experts, give educators a free zero-install classroom activity, and inspire interest in mission design and space careers.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE
Instead of explaining trade-offs in a lecture, we made the trade-offs the gameplay itself. Players learn by designing, failing, and improving, alone, as a team around one screen, or against other teams online.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED
Accessibility (plays in any browser, on desktop or mobile, with no sign-up), clarity for beginners, short play sessions, a gradual difficulty curve across the five stages, both solo and group play so it works in classrooms and at home, and keeping the concepts faithful to how NASA-style missions are planned.

OUR TEAM’S ROLE
Our team conceived the game and wrote detailed specifications and instructions at the start of the project, defining the concept, goals, target audience, gameplay flow, game modes, stage structure, and the overall design and look of the game. We directed the AI tools through these instructions and further iterations, then tested the game and reviewed, selected, and approved the final result.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES
A web application built with web technologies. The front end is hosted on Cloudflare Pages and is accessible through a single public link. A game server [Node.js / other] handles the online modes and the leaderboard, [using WebSockets / other] for real-time play.

USE OF AI
This project was built with extensive use of AI tools (large language models such as Claude). Following detailed specifications and design direction written by our team, AI was used to generate the game’s code and written content, including the text of this submission. The concept and design direction came from our team.
